pages.text: A $(item)Descriptive Book$() is a door that dreams of a world. The first time it opens, the Age answers. A $(item)Linking Book$() is humbler and wiser: it remembers one exact place and begs the path to return there.

Both books now keep a small painted remembrance when they can. If the leaves hold a true survey card, you may study it before crossing. If not, the binding falls back to sky and mist alone until a better likeness is taken.

When first awakened, a descriptive book reads its pages, takes its chosen name, and sets you at an arrival ground it believes survivable. Still, trust boots before faith. Stone has swallowed better travelers than I.

A linking book opens to that same remembrance instead of yanking you away at once. Touch its panel to cross, or refresh the painted scene if the place has changed. Those in a hurry may still crouch and use the book to leap without ceremony.

Never forget what the book truly is. A descriptive book is not only a key but the bound heart of the Age. In survival, each crossing leaves that heart behind as an anchored volume at the place of departure. Even a book dropped by hand will assume the same resting shape. Take it back by hand if you mean to move it. Strike it down only if you are prepared to trust the loose book to fate.

Should you die in an Age with no safer bed sworn to you, the Age may call you back to itself. Therefore the wise carry a spare linking book, or build a crystal road home before pride begins making decisions.
A sacrificed Age is not merely distant. It is dead. Ordinary travelers are cast out, and its links weep unreadable ink. Only those who walk as ghosts or makers may inspect the hollow that remains.
